input.rationale: Section 12 is the only indemnity in the Agreement. Section 12(b) (p0073/p0075) limits TrueLink's indemnity to "any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations or agreements hereunder" — it contains no third-party IP infringement cover, no duty to defend, and no claims procedure, and TrueLink gives no non-infringement warranty (its only warranties, in Section 9, are Y2K, and p0076 disclaims all others), so nothing else supplies IP protection. Meanwhile Section 12(a) (p0071/p0072) imposes a very broad Client indemnity covering any Client breach, Web Site/Client Content claims and third-party product/service injury. That fails the fallback's first element (Vendor IP indemnity), so this is a deviation, not a clause sitting at the fallback. We target the preferred position rather than the fallback because the fallback's 3× super-cap would import a cap into an indemnity that is presently uncapped (the p0077 cap reaches only Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11), and the preferred route requires no cap language. Operation 1 inserts a TrueLink indemnity (IP infringement of the Interface, Hosting Services or Support Services; breach of applicable law; TrueLink-caused unauthorised access to Client Content or Credit Data; gross negligence or willful misconduct) with notice, control-of-defence and cooperation mechanics; operation 2 narrows the Client indemnity to Client Content and Client's violations of law.

proposal.summary: Add TrueLink indemnity for third-party IP, breach of law, data breach and gross negligence/wilful misconduct with standard procedure, and narrow the Client indemnity.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] TrueLink's indemnity in Section 12(b) covers only its own breach of this Agreement, so we have added a vendor indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of applicable law, TrueLink-caused data breach and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice, control-of-defence and cooperation mechanics, and narrowed our indemnity to Client Content and our own violations of law. If preferred, we can discuss the fallback of an IP-only indemnity with customary exclusions and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies.

ops.text: TrueLink shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Client and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Interface, Hosting Services or Support Services infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (ii) TrueLink's breach of applicable law; (iii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or Credit Data caused by TrueLink; or (iv) TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct. Each indemnity under this Section 12 is conditioned on the indemnified party giving prompt written notice of the claim, the indemnifying party having control of the defense of the claim, and the indemnified party providing reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

ops.oldText: (i) any claim arising out of any breach by Client of this Agreement, (ii) any claim or demand resulting from any act or omission by Client or any customer of Client granted access to the Interface by Client which constitutes a breach of or default by TrueLink under any System Agreement or Credit Repository Agreement, which breach or default has either not been cured or cannot be cured within the applicable cure period and the consequences of which is that TrueLink will lose material rights it has pursuant to said Agreements or a violation of any state or federal law, rule or regulation (iii) any claim arising out of or relating to the Web Site or Client Content (including, but not limited to, any claim resulting from any content posted to the Web Site by Client or Client's employees, agent or any customer of Client granted access to the Interface by Client), without regard to any knowledge limitation or qualification that may be contained in this Agreement, and (iv) injury or damage to person or property caused by a product, service, or information, whether or not defective, that is sold, distributed or transmitted from the Web Site.
ops.newText: (i) any claim arising out of or relating to Client Content provided by Client, and (ii) any violation by Client of applicable state or federal law, rule or regulation.
